pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: The urine turning a dark port-wine color following light exposure, coupled with severe abdominal pain out of proportion to physical exam, autonomic instability, and rapid-onset motor neuropathy triggered by caloric restriction. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant inborn error of heme biosynthesis caused by a deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBG-D). Caloric deprivation (fasting/ketosis) and porphyrogenic medications induce hepatic delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase 1 (ALAS1). In the setting of impaired PBG-D, this leads to the catastrophic accumulation of upstream, neurotoxic heme precursors: delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). Oxidation and polymerization of excess PBG into porphobilin when exposed to ambient light causes the pathognomonic port-wine color change. The neurotoxicity of ALA causes visceral autonomic neuropathy (severe abdominal pain, hypertension, tachycardia, ileus), central nervous system dysfunction (psychosis, seizures, SIADH causing hyponatremia), and motor axonal neuropathy (predominantly proximal and upper-limb motor weakness leading to respiratory failure).
